g.data-info: A layer of fat cells beneath the dermis that insulates the body, stores energy and cushions it.
A thick layer of connective tissue with collagen and elastic fibres containing blood vessels, glands, nerves and hair follicles.
The outer protective layer of skin made of layers of cells that are constantly replaced from below.
The outermost layer of dead, flattened, keratin-filled cells that forms a waterproof barrier.
The deepest layer of the epidermis, where cells divide by mitosis to replace those lost from the surface.
Arterioles, capillaries and venules supplying the skin; they widen or narrow to help control body temperature.
A pit of epidermal cells reaching into the dermis, with a bulb at its base where the hair grows.
The dead, keratinised part of the hair that projects above the skin surface.
A gland that secretes oily sebum into the hair follicle to keep the hair and skin soft and waterproof.
A tiny smooth muscle that contracts to pull the hair upright, trapping a layer of air (goosebumps).
A coiled tube that secretes sweat; evaporation of sweat cools the body.
The duct carries sweat up through the dermis and epidermis to open at a pore on the skin surface.
A pressure receptor made of onion-like layers around a nerve ending, deep in the skin.
